input.title: Client-side hashing was chosen over three alternatives because it keeps the ref in document state bit-identical to a server-issued ref

input.description: Reservation-keyed and provisional refs break ref equality for identical content or make the reservation table permanent; deferring dispatch leaves collaborators and processors blind until upload ends.

input.content:
The hash-first design lets a client compute the SHA-256 itself, build the ref immediately, submit the action, and upload afterwards. Four approaches were evaluated — client-side hashing, a dual-nature scalar carrying a reservation id that later resolves to a hash, provisional refs with a second-phase link step, and pure client-side orchestration (defer dispatch until the upload completes) — and client-side hashing won on four counts:

- **Content-addressing and dedup survive end to end.** Two clients attaching the same file independently produce the *same ref string* in document state. Reservation-keyed or provisional refs permanently break ref equality for identical content.
- **No resolution layer.** Reservation-keyed refs would turn a transient table into permanent, must-sync, must-never-lose mapping infrastructure, because operations are immutable and the refs inside them would depend on that table forever.
- **No new actions, no reducer or codegen changes.** A link step needs a new base action, adds an operation per upload to the document log, and strands the document in a provisional state if the link is lost.
- **The action is durable immediately.** Deferring dispatch improves perceived latency but fails the actual requirement: collaborators, sync peers and server-side processors see nothing until the upload finishes.

Two existing facts made it nearly free. The browser upload path **already buffers the whole file** (`RemoteAttachmentUpload.send()` collects the stream into a Blob because streaming request bodies are not universally supported), so hashing is one `crypto.subtle.digest("SHA-256", …)` over memory already paid for — and `crypto.subtle` is already a dependency for operation signing. And the architecture already tolerates a ref without local data; what is new is tolerating a ref before *any* reactor has the data, a difference in degree.

Node and CLI clients hash with `crypto.createHash("sha256")` over a first streaming pass. A caller with a true one-shot stream simply omits the client hash and gets the upload-first flow — both modes coexist on the same interfaces.
